items.title: 53279_Lee Young Oral History Interview
items.q: I'll tell you who made the arrangements for us -- Gerald Wilson was making arrangements for us, Dudley Brooks, and Billy Strayhorn.

ctx.x: And so -- as I stated before, they thought that I was gonna axe Bumps and have Lester in the band, but I intended to have both of them in the band.

So they wouldn't allow Lester to play with the band when he first arrived, and they told him that he had to appear as a guest; he could play three sets a night --but he had to play on the floor, he couldn't play on the bandstand with the band. And so he would come to Billy Berg's, and he had a little; he would set out back all night on a milk box waiting to come on, and we would play a set; we would play 3 sets a night, and then we would introduce Lester Young, and he'd come out and stand in the middle of the…

items.title: 53279_Lee Young Oral History Interview
items.q: the band that we had was quite unique... this was why Gerald and Dudley and Billy Strayon wanted to write for us

ctx.x: Okay. So the band that we had was quite unique because they had not started using guitars playing parts, so we had 4 part harmony, and this was why Gerald and Dudley and Billy Strayon wanted to write for us, because we had -- which is a big sound; he used a trumpet, 2 tenors and guitar. And you voice that properly, and you have a big sound -- and we did have a big sound.
As a matter of fact, we made so much noise out here, they heard about it back east, and they brought -- Barney Josephson brought us back there to work Cafe Society.
